The twelve-bar blues is three four-bar phrases on three chords. Almost everything players
have done to it since is one of a small number of moves: go to a chord sooner, approach a
chord with its own dominant, split a dominant into a two-five, or replace a dominant with
the one a tritone away. This lesson adds those moves one at a time. The site's backing band
plays every chart on this page, so you can hear each change as it arrives.

**How to use the page.** Press ▶ on any chart and the band plays two choruses after a
one-bar count-in. Section 8 has a tune written in notation, where the note that is sounding
lights up. The bar that is sounding lights up. The strip at the bottom of the window
sets the key, the feel, the tempo and the chord instrument for the whole page, and you can
change them while the band plays. Under every chord is its Roman numeral, which stays the
same in every key.

## 1. The three-chord blues

Four bars of **I**, two of **IV** and two of **I**, then **V**, **IV**, **I**, **I**. Every
chord is a dominant seventh, including the home chord. That is the sound of the blues: a
tonic that carries a flat seventh and does not need to resolve.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="basic"></div>

Listen for the two places the form turns. Bar 5 is the first move away from home. Bar 9 is
the highest point of tension, and the last four bars walk it back down.

## 2. The quick change and the turnaround

Two small changes, both very common. In bar 2 the band goes to **IV** for one bar and comes
straight back (the *quick change*), which breaks up four bars of the same chord. In bar 12
the band plays **V** instead of resting on I, so the end of the chorus pulls into the top of
the next one (a *turnaround*).

<div class="bl-step" data-step="quick"></div>

Use **Hear it without the changes** to compare with the chart before. The shaded bars are
the ones that differ.

## 3. The jazz blues: a two-five in the last line

Swing and bebop players turned the last line round. Instead of V then IV, they play
**ii7** then **V7**: the bass now moves by fifths (G, C, F in the key of F) all the way home.
To set up the ii chord, bar 8 becomes **VI7**, the dominant of ii. The turnaround in bars
11 and 12 is the same idea at twice the speed: I, VI7, ii7, V7, two beats each.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="jazz"></div>

## 4. Getting to IV, and getting back

Three more moves, each of them a way to make an arrival stronger.

- **Bar 4**: a two-five into IV. The I7 chord in bar 4 is already the dominant of IV, so put
  its ii chord in front of it (**v7 I7**, two beats each).
- **Bar 6**: the bass climbs a half step from IV to **♯iv°7**, and that chord pulls back
  to I in bar 7. This one is as old as the blues on the piano.
- **Bar 8**: split VI7 into its own two-five, **iii7 VI7**.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="approach"></div>

## 5. Tritone substitution

A dominant seventh chord and the dominant seventh a tritone away share the same third and
seventh (swapped). So either can stand in for the other, and the substitute's root arrives
by a half step from above instead of by a fifth. Here it is in four places: the end of bar 4
(**♯IV7** falling to IV), the end of bar 8 (**♭III7** falling to ii), bar 10 (**♭II7** falling
to I), and a turnaround built entirely of substitutes: I, ♭III7, ♭VI7, ♭II7.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="tritone"></div>

Listen to the bass. Wherever a substitute is used, the line slides down by half step.

## 6. The Bird blues

Charlie Parker's "Blues for Alice" keeps only three landmarks of the form: I in bar 1, IV in
bar 5 and the two-five in bars 9 and 10. Everything between is a chain of two-fives. Bars 2
to 4 descend by step to reach IV. Bars 6 to 9 descend by half step to reach ii. The home
chord is a major seventh, not a dominant.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="bird"></div>

Compare it with the jazz blues of section 3. The shaded bars show how little is left.

## 7. The minor blues

The same twelve bars with minor i and iv chords. The last line is usually **♭VI7** to
**V7**: a dominant a half step above the dominant (the tritone substitute of V's own
dominant). The turnaround uses a half-diminished ii chord. "Mr. P.C." and
"Equinox" are both built this way.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="minor"></div>

## 8. A tune on these changes: Blues in the Closet

Oscar Pettiford's *Blues in the Closet* is a good first tune because its changes are the
three-chord blues with just two of the moves above.

- **Bars 9 and 10** are a two-five, **ii7 then V7**, as in the jazz blues of section 3.
- **Bar 12** is **V7**, the turnaround of section 2.

Everything else is plain. There is no quick change in bar 2 (four full bars of I), bars 5
and 6 are IV, bars 7 and 8 stay on I with no VI7, and bar 11 is one bar of I. The shaded
bars are the ones that differ from the three-chord blues of section 1.

<div class="bl-step" data-step="closet"></div>

The melody is one two-bar riff played three times, and the note that is sounding lights up
as it plays. Listen to bars 5 and 6: one note of the riff is a half step lower there than
in bars 1 and 2, because the 3rd of the I chord has become the ♭7th of the IV chord. The
changes are in the melody. In bars 9 and 10 the riff does not change at all, even though
the chords under it are new: every note of it belongs to both the ii chord and the V
chord.

To build this chorus yourself in the next section, choose *Stay on I*, *Stay on I*,
*Stay on IV*, *Stay on I*, *Two-five* and *V in the last bar*. **Open in the Backing Track**
puts the tune on that page in a new tab, where the bass line, comping and drums can each be
chosen. The instrument lessons each
end with this tune, and [the improvising lesson](blues-improv.qmd) is built on it.

## Build your own chorus

Choose one option for each pair of bars and the chart rewrites itself. Change a menu while
the band is playing and the new chords come in at the next bar. All of the options fit
together, so there is no wrong combination: try the plainest first line with the busiest
turnaround, or the reverse.

<div id="bl-builder" class="bl-widget"></div>

## Test your ear

The band plays a plain blues with one pair of bars changed. The question tells you which
bars to listen to; the counter shows where the band is. Pick what you heard.

<div id="bl-quiz" class="bl-widget"></div>

## Where to go next

- Play along. Set the strip at the bottom to **Loop**, pick a key and improvise over each
  version in turn. Bars 4, 8 and 12 are where the new chords ask for new notes.
- Take a chorus you built to **Tools → Backing Track** (use *Copy as ABC* above and paste it
  into *Edit the changes (ABC)* there) to choose the bass line, comping rhythm and drum groove part
  by part.
- Learn each version in the keys you play most: F and B♭ for horns, E, A and G for guitar.

    { from: 8,  opts: [['V then IV', 'C7|Bb7'], ['Two bars of V', 'C7|C7'], ['Two-five', 'Gm7|C7'], ['Two, then the tritone substitute', 'Gm7|Gb7']] },

  ];
  var FEELS = [{ id: 'swing', label: 'Medium swing', tempo: 120 }, { id: 'doowop', label: 'Slow blues in 12/8', tempo: 60 }, { id: 'boogaloo', label: 'Straight-eighth boogaloo', tempo: 116 }];

    for (var i = 0; i < out.length; i += 4) rows.push(out.slice(i, i + 4).join(' | '));

    $('bl-stop').disabled = true; status('');
  }
  function stop() { if (player) { try { player.stop(); } catch (e) {} } idle(); }
  // view = whatever shows the sounding bar (setLive); cycle = [from, to] form bars to go round, to < from = over the end
  // tune = a makeTune() whose melody the band's piano plays over the chart (written pitch less the key: the player adds the key back)
  function withTune(parsed, tune) { if (tune) parsed.bars.forEach(function (pb, i) { var m = tune.bars[i]; if (m && m.length) pb.melody = m.map(function (n) { return { pos: n.pos, dur: n.dur, midi: n.midi - semis() }; }); }); return parsed; }

    var parsed = withTune(TuneChart.parse(abcOf(bars, minor)), tune), b = band(); b.opts.melody = !!tune; b.opts.melodyLevel = 0.95;
    if (!player) player = window.BandPlayer.create({ parsed: parsed, tempo: state.tempo, transpose: semis(), countIn: 1, opts: b.opts, instruments: b.instruments,
      onBar: function (info) { if (!now) return; status(info.countIn ? 'Count-in' : info.ending ? '' : 'Bar ' + (info.index + 1) + (state.loop || now.cycle ? '' : ', chorus ' + (info.chorus + 1) + ' of 2'));
        if (now.view) now.view.setLive(info.countIn || info.ending ? -1 : info.index); },
      onState: function (s) { if (s === 'loading') status('Loading the sounds…'); },
      onEnd: idle });
    else { player.setInstruments(b.instruments); player.setChart(parsed); player.setOpts(b.opts); player.setTempo(state.tempo); player.setTranspose(semis()); }
    player.setCycle(cycle ? cycle[0] : null, cycle ? cycle[1] : null);
    player.setStartBar(cycle ? cycle[0] : 0);
    player.setChoruses(cycle || state.loop ? 0 : 2);
    now = { btn: btn, label: btn.textContent, view: view, cycle: cycle, tune: tune || null, bars: bars, minor: minor };
    btn.textContent = '■ Stop'; btn.classList.add('bl-on'); $('bl-stop').disabled = false;
    player.play().then(function () { if (now && now.btn === btn) window.requestAnimationFrame(follow); }, function () { idle(); status('The sounds could not be loaded.'); });
  }
  function playBtn(label, primary) { var b = el('button', 'btn btn-sm ' + (primary ? 'btn-primary' : 'btn-outline-secondary'), label); b.type = 'button'; return b; }

  // ---- the numbered sections ----
  Array.prototype.forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('.bl-step'), function (host) {
    var s = STEPS[host.getAttribute('data-step')]; if (!s) return;
    var bars = split(s.bars), before = s.prev ? split(STEPS[s.prev].bars) : null;
    var changed = before ? bars.map(function (b, i) { return b !== before[i] ? i : -1; }).filter(function (i) { return i >= 0; }) : [];
    host.classList.add('bl-widget');
    var tools = el('div', 'bl-tools'), paper = el('div'); host.appendChild(paper);
    var view = makeChart(paper, bars, s.minor, changed), tune = s.tune ? makeTune(host, s.tune, paper) : null;
    host.insertBefore(tools, paper);                                            // the play buttons sit directly above the chord grid, below the tune's own staff
    var b1 = playBtn(tune ? '▶ Play with the band' : '▶ Play', true); b1.addEventListener('click', function () { play(b1, view, bars, s.minor, null, tune); }); tools.appendChild(b1);
    if (tune && tune.open) { tune.open.className = 'btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary'; tools.appendChild(tune.open); }
    if (before) { var b2 = playBtn('▶ Hear it without the changes'); b2.addEventListener('click', function () { play(b2, view, before, s.minor); }); tools.appendChild(b2); }
    if (s.loop) { var to = s.loop[1], b3 = playBtn('▶ Loop bars ' + (s.loop[0] + 1) + (to < s.loop[0] ? ' to 12 and on into bar ' : ' to ') + (to + 1));
      b3.addEventListener('click', function () { play(b3, view, bars, s.minor, s.loop); }); tools.appendChild(b3); }
    if (changed.length) { var lg = el('p', 'bl-legend'); lg.appendChild(el('i')); lg.appendChild(document.createTextNode('Changed from the version before')); host.appendChild(lg); }
  });

  // ---- build your own ----
  function assemble(picks) { var out = []; SLOTS.forEach(function (sl, k) { out = out.concat(split(sl.opts[picks[k]][1])); }); return out; }
  function optionLabel(o) { return o[0] + ':  ' + numerals(split(o[1])); }
  (function () {
    var host = $('bl-builder'); if (!host) return;
    var picks = SLOTS.map(function () { return 0; }), grid = el('div', 'bl-slots'), tools = el('div', 'bl-tools'), paper = el('div'), sels = [];
    host.appendChild(grid); host.appendChild(tools); host.appendChild(paper);
    var view = makeChart(paper, assemble(picks), false, []);
    function marked() { var m = []; SLOTS.forEach(function (sl, k) { if (picks[k]) m.push(sl.from, sl.from + 1); }); return m; }
    function refresh() {
      view.set(assemble(picks), marked());
      if (now && now.view === view && player) player.setChart(TuneChart.parse(abcOf(view.bars, false)));
    }
    SLOTS.forEach(function (sl, k) {
      var wrap = el('div'), id = 'bl-slot-' + k, lab = el('label', null, 'Bars ' + (sl.from + 1) + ' and ' + (sl.from + 2)), sel = el('select', 'form-select form-select-sm');
      lab.htmlFor = id; sel.id = id;
      sl.opts.forEach(function (o, i) { var op = el('option', null, optionLabel(o)); op.value = i; sel.appendChild(op); });
      sel.addEventListener('change', function () { picks[k] = +sel.value; refresh(); });
      wrap.appendChild(lab); wrap.appendChild(sel); grid.appendChild(wrap); sels.push(sel);
    });
    function setAll(fn) { picks = SLOTS.map(fn); sels.forEach(function (s, k) { s.value = picks[k]; }); refresh(); }
    var go = playBtn('▶ Play', true); go.addEventListener('click', function () { play(go, view, view.bars, false); }); tools.appendChild(go);
    var rnd = playBtn('Surprise me'); rnd.addEventListener('click', function () { setAll(function (sl) { return Math.floor(Math.random() * sl.opts.length); }); }); tools.appendChild(rnd);
    var plain = playBtn('Back to three chords'); plain.addEventListener('click', function () { setAll(function () { return 0; }); }); tools.appendChild(plain);
    var copy = playBtn('Copy as ABC'); tools.appendChild(copy);
    copy.addEventListener('click', function () {
      var text = abcOf(view.bars, false).replace('T:Blues', 'T:My blues (written in F)');
      var done = function (ok) { copy.textContent = ok ? 'Copied' : 'Could not copy'; setTimeout(function () { copy.textContent = 'Copy as ABC'; }, 1500); };
      if (navigator.clipboard && navigator.clipboard.writeText) navigator.clipboard.writeText(text).then(function () { done(true); }, function () { done(false); }); else done(false);
    });
    var lg = el('p', 'bl-legend'); lg.appendChild(el('i')); lg.appendChild(document.createTextNode('Changed from the three-chord blues')); host.appendChild(lg);
  })();

  // ---- test your ear ----
  (function () {
    var host = $('bl-quiz'); if (!host) return;
    var tools = el('div', 'bl-tools'), ask = el('p', null, 'Press New question to begin.'), count = el('div', 'bl-count'), answers = el('div', 'bl-answers'),
        verdict = el('p', 'bl-verdict'), score = el('p', 'bl-score'), paper = el('div');
    [tools, ask, count, answers, verdict, score, paper].forEach(function (e) { host.appendChild(e); });
    paper.hidden = true; verdict.setAttribute('aria-live', 'polite');
    var boxes = []; for (var i = 0; i < 12; i++) { var d = el('div', null, String(i + 1)); count.appendChild(d); boxes.push(d); }
    var counter = { setLive: function (i) { boxes.forEach(function (b, k) { b.classList.toggle('bl-live', k === i); }); } };
    var q = null, right = 0, asked = 0, last = -1, reveal = null;
    var next = playBtn('New question', true), again = playBtn('▶ Hear it again'); again.disabled = true; tools.appendChild(next); tools.appendChild(again);
    function listen() { if (q) play(again, counter, q.bars, false); }
    again.addEventListener('click', listen);
    next.addEventListener('click', function () {
      var k; do { k = Math.floor(Math.random() * SLOTS.length); } while (k === last); last = k;
      var sl = SLOTS[k], picks = SLOTS.map(function () { return 0; }); picks[k] = Math.floor(Math.random() * sl.opts.length);
      q = { slot: k, pick: picks[k], bars: assemble(picks), done: false };
      ask.textContent = 'Listen to bars ' + (sl.from + 1) + ' and ' + (sl.from + 2) + '. Which do you hear?';
      boxes.forEach(function (b, i) { b.classList.toggle('bl-ask', i === sl.from || i === sl.from + 1); });
      answers.textContent = ''; verdict.textContent = ''; paper.hidden = true; again.disabled = false;
      sl.opts.forEach(function (o, i) {
        var b = el('button', 'btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary', optionLabel(o)); b.type = 'button';
        b.addEventListener('click', function () {
          if (q.done) return; q.done = true; asked++;
          var ok = i === q.pick; if (ok) right++; else b.classList.add('bl-wrong');
          answers.children[q.pick].classList.add('bl-right');
          verdict.textContent = ok ? 'Yes.' : 'Not this time. The band played "' + sl.opts[q.pick][0] + '".';
          score.textContent = right + ' right out of ' + asked;
          paper.hidden = false;
          if (!reveal) reveal = makeChart(paper, q.bars, false, [sl.from, sl.from + 1]); else reveal.set(q.bars, [sl.from, sl.from + 1]);
        });
        answers.appendChild(b);
      });
      if (now && now.btn === again) stop();
      listen();
    });
  })();

  // ---- the strip at the bottom ----
  KEYS.forEach(function (k, i) { var o = el('option', null, k); o.value = i; $('bl-key').appendChild(o); });
  FEELS.forEach(function (f) { var o = el('option', null, f.label); o.value = f.id; $('bl-feel').appendChild(o); });
  function showTempo() { $('bl-tempo').value = state.tempo; $('bl-tempo-n').value = state.tempo; }
  function setTempo(v) { v = Math.max(40, Math.min(220, Math.round(+v) || state.tempo)); state.tempo = v; showTempo(); if (player) player.setTempo(v); }
  function setBand() { if (!player) return; var b = band(); player.setInstruments(b.instruments); player.setOpts(b.opts); }
  $('bl-key').value = state.key; $('bl-feel').value = state.feel; showTempo();
  $('bl-key').addEventListener('change', function () { state.key = +this.value; charts.forEach(function (c) { c.rekey(); }); tunes.forEach(function (t) { t.draw(); });
    if (player) { player.setTranspose(semis()); if (now && now.tune) player.setChart(withTune(TuneChart.parse(abcOf(now.bars, now.minor)), now.tune)); } });
  $('bl-feel').addEventListener('change', function () { state.feel = this.value; var f = FEELS.filter(function (x) { return x.id === state.feel; })[0]; setBand(); setTempo(f.tempo); });
  $('bl-inst').addEventListener('change', function () { state.inst = this.value; setBand(); });
  $('bl-tempo').addEventListener('input', function () { setTempo(this.value); });
  $('bl-tempo-n').addEventListener('change', function () { setTempo(this.value); });
  $('bl-loop').addEventListener('change', function () { state.loop = this.checked; if (player && now && !now.cycle) player.setChoruses(state.loop ? 0 : 2); });
  $('bl-stop').addEventListener('click', stop);
})();
</script>
